title: Geographic Routing, Resilience, and Energy-SLA Alignment Guidelines
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This guideline defines design principles, operational requirements, and implementation patterns for geographically aware request routing, multi-region failover topologies, and alignment of energy/cost SLAs for Redwood inference services. The goal is to give product and infra teams a concrete, repeatable playbook to build resilient, cost- and energy-conscious routing while honoring latency and availability SLOs.

Why this doc exists:
- Reduce cross-region flapping and unsafe cutovers during outages.
- Ensure energy and cost accounting are first-class signals used for routing decisions (not just quotas).
- Provide a standard failover matrix and rollout steps for region-level incidents.
- Align runtime placement decisions with business tiering (hosted/dedicated/private).

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood public API edge, regional ingress proxies, and the runtime placement decision layer (smart router).
- Includes policies for hosted API, Dedicated clusters, and Private/VPC deployments where Redwood controls the control plane.
- Excludes: customer-managed on-prem routing (see Private deployment runbook).

Key goals and constraints:
1) Latency-first steering: Prefer local-region serving when median p95 latency delta <= 75ms and SLOs not violated.
2) Energy-aware fallback: When a region enters an energy-constraint mode (quota reached or scheduled demand response), route to cheapest compatible region consistent with SLO tiers.
3) Predictable degradation: During sustained capacity events, degrade by fidelity tiers (quantized variant -> smaller context -> best-effort) rather than unbounded latency.
4) Observability and auditability: Every cross-region reroute must be annotated with reason codes and tie back to a causal event id.

Architecture overview (text diagram):

  [Edge] -> [Region Router A] -> [Regional Ingress Proxy] -> [Runtime Pool R-A]
                       |
                       +-> [Region Router B] -> [Regional Ingress Proxy] -> [Runtime Pool R-B]
                       |
                       +-> [Control Plane Smart Router (global)]

The Control Plane Smart Router evaluates per-request hints (tenant, SLO tier, cost-sensitivity hint, energy budget flag) to decide whether to serve locally, route to remote region, or invoke fallback model variant.

Routing inputs and hints (ordered by precedence):
- Client-provided preference header: X-Redwood-Region (explicit pin) - honored only for private deployments or dedicated clusters unless tenant policy allows.
- Tenant tier (from token metadata): {free, standard, enterprise, dedicated}.
- SLO class in request: {interactive, bulk, background}.
- Energy/cost signal: regional_energy_state={normal, constrained, throttled}, region_cost_index (float).
- Health signals: p50/p95 latency, error_rate, available_gpu_units.

Policy decision matrix (high-level):
- If region_health == healthy and latency_budget available: serve local.
- If region_health == degraded and tenant is enterprise/dedicated AND dedicated_capacity_available -> route to tenant-dedicated pool in another region in same jurisdiction.
- If energy_state == constrained AND tenant_allows_cost_fallback -> route to next-cheapest compatible region prioritizing same legal jurisdiction.
- If model_variant downgrade is configured and will preserve SLO, prefer downgrade in-region before cross-region hop.

SLOs and operational thresholds (concrete):
- Interactive tier: p95 latency <= 250ms, availability >= 99.9% (monthly).
- Bulk tier: p95 latency <= 1.2s, availability >= 99.5% (monthly).
- Regional failure detection: mark degraded when sustained p95 > 2x SLO for 2 minutes OR error_rate > 2% for 5 minutes.
- Cross-region failover trigger: when degraded persists for 3 minutes AND available_gpu_units < 25% for 2 consecutive checks (1m cadence).

Failover matrix (ASCII table):

| Incident type            | Immediate local action                     | Next region action                            | Fallback variant         |
|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| Thermal/energy constraint| Throttle batch sizes; mark energy_constrained| Move non-interactive to remote; limit burst   | Lower-precision quantized|
| Network partition (ingress)| Pause new canaries; keep steady for live traffic| Route interactive to nearest healthy region | Canary model (smaller context)|
| GPU hardware loss        | Drain connections; shift active sessions     | Rebalance to sibling shards in region or remote| Best-effort small context |

Implementation checklist (step-by-step):
1) Add routing hints to the edge request envelope: region_hint, cost_sensitivity, energy_aware boolean.
2) Implement regional_energy_state export: metric name redwood.region.energy_state with tags region, window.
3) Control Plane Smart Router must implement a weighted-scorer: 0.6*latency_score + 0.3*cost_score + 0.1*jurisdiction_penalty. Scores normalized to [0,1].
4) Annotate every routed response with X-Redwood-Routed-From and X-Redwood-Decision-Reason.
5) Wire automated rollback: if remote-route p95 > local_SLO_margin for 5 minutes, return routing to local (with alert).

Sample config table (acceptable defaults):

| config_key                           | default           | notes                                            |
|--------------------------------------|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| routing.latency_weight               | 0.6               | weight in scoring function                       |
| routing.cost_weight                  | 0.3               | prefer cheaper region for non-interactive traffic|
| routing.jurisdiction_penalty         | 0.1               | penalize cross-jurisdiction hops                 |
| energy.alert_threshold_pct           | 80                | region energy budget percent to flip to constrained|
| failover.remote_cooldown_seconds     | 300               | min time to wait before reversing a remote route |

Rollout and canary playbook (numbered):
1. Feature branch: implement hint headers and scoring in a feature flag guarded service (router.v3).
2. Unit + integration tests: include synthetic latency/cost inputs and assert deterministic routing decisions.
3. Canary region: enable for 5% of traffic in staging region for 24 hours. Collect metrics: routed_fraction, p95_remote_vs_local, error_rate_delta.
4. Gradual expansion: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 72 hours, pause at each step for 2x alert window.
5. Full rollout: apply to global edge after successful 7-day observation period.

Monitoring, alerting, and dashboards:
- Dashboards: Region overview (p50/p95/error_rate/energy_state) and Routing decisions heatmap (by tenant tier).
- Key alerts: RegionDegraded (trigger when detection threshold met), UnintendedCrossRegionSurge (>5% unexpected cross-region traffic for 15m), EnergyFailoverRatio (>30% of non-bulk requests routed for energy reasons).
- Logs: All decision traces must be indexed with request_id and decision_reason for 60 days.

Security and compliance notes:
- Cross-jurisdiction routing must honor data residency labels on tenant tokens. If tenant.residency == "EU-only" then jurisdiction_penalty = 1.0 and cross-region routing outside EU is forbidden.
- Annotate routing decisions in audit logs for enterprise customers with retention flags required by contracts.

Operational runbook (short):
1. When RegionDegraded fires: confirm metric causality via region overview dashboard.
2. If degraded == energy_constrained: enable energy_fallback mode to limit interactive re-routes to enterprise/dedicated tiers only.
3. Communicate via internal status channel and update status page if availability SLO impacted.
4. After recovery, runcing (post-incident) report with counts of cross-region requests and energy vs hardware causes.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Primary: Edge & Routing team (owner: Diego Alvarez) — implement scoring and decision telemetry.
- Secondary: Serving Runtime (owner: Anika Rao) — ensure model downgrade variants available and safe.
- SRE: maintain dashboards, alerts, and runbooks (owner: Priya Kapoor).

Appendix A — Example scoring pseudo-YAML: 

scorer:
  weights:
    latency: 0.6
    cost: 0.3
    jurisdiction_penalty: 0.1
  normalize_to: 1.0
  compute_interval_seconds: 60

Appendix B — Example request header snippet:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n  -H 'X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2' \n  -H 'X-Redwood-Cost-Sensitivity: low' \n  -d '{"input":"..."}'

- See gpu-energy-proportional-scheduler-design-and-billing-playbook for GPU-side energy interactions.
